answer: A staged-reveal bond blocks bulk fake identities. Each agent posts an onyx seal, a hash of one unique work artifact, and locks a 20-unit bond. A juniper checkpoint opens randomly, and the agent reveals the matching artifact with fresh proof. Auditors check reuse; a mismatch burns the bond and raises the spiral tier for that funder, so the k-th fake costs 20 plus 9k units and 1,000 fakes cost 4,524,500 units, since burned bonds cannot be reposted. Rented samples fail since the artifact is already sealed. An honest agent posts once, passes once, and recovers the bond.
